keyVerseText: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head: white: or, full of holes
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun סַל (çal) derives from the root סָלַל (çâlal), which carries the fundamental idea of lifting up or raising. This root involves actions such as casting up a highway or mound, or figuratively exalting or making something prominent. The root sense of lifting or raising adds a vivid image to the common English gloss 'basket,' suggesting not merely a container but something woven and elevated, perhaps symbolizing care and provision raised up for use or display.
usageInScripture: The word סַל appears 15 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently translated as 'basket' or 'baskets,' emphasizing its role as a woven container. The occurrences include singular and plural forms, as well as phrases like 'out of the basket' and 'that is in the basket,' indicating its practical use in daily life and ritual contexts. This consistency highlights the basket as a tangible object associated with carrying, holding, or presenting items, often in a sacred or significant setting.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding סַל as a basket woven from willow twigs and elevated by its root meaning enriches our appreciation of biblical imagery where provision, care, and divine ordering are symbolized. The basket is not just a mundane object but one that can carry God's blessings or judgments, as seen in various ritual and narrative scenes. The idea of lifting up inherent in the root reminds believers of God's exaltation of the lowly and His provision raised up for His people. Thus, the basket can serve as a metaphor for God’s sustaining grace and the faithful stewardship of His gifts.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 40:16, the chief baker recounts his dream of having 'three white baskets on my head,' a vivid image that uses the word סַל to convey a container placed overhead, signifying burden or responsibility. The term 'basket' here is not merely a physical object but a symbol within the dream's divine revelation. Recognizing סַל as a woven, elevated basket deepens the understanding of the baker's experience and the unfolding of God's sovereign plan through Joseph's gift of interpretation.
